longscout.note: research/longscout_v1.py frozen at this commit; master strategies.py/backtest.py of #340 base

rule: Codex catalog-and-sieve rule v1 exactly as in sieve_v1.py / sieve_v1_panel.py (max one position, $8 risk on a $3,333.33 notional cap = the $4,000-account proxy, 40 coin orders, path scenario decides, worst path is a diagnostic). Gates (medians over 40 orders): n >= 100 closes, meanR15 > 0, meanR23 >= 0, both halves (split 2025-01-01) meanR15 > 0, meanR15 without the best coin > 0, order 0 >= 30 closes per half. Status TRANSFER_SCREEN_PASS only when all hold.
secondary: post-hoc max 3 / max 5 only as labelled secondary evidence, never a pass
universe: extra31 (the 31 coins outside the original nine); BTC is context only
multiple_testing: 8 new candidates are run at once; about one false pass in that many is plausible, so a pass is a lead for Codex reproduction and a forward test, never an activation
never: no gate weakened, no parameter tuned, no coin dropped to rescue a candidate; a changed rule is a new candidate

regime_check.question: owner: is exp_trend's short bias real market-structure reading or luck?
regime_check.rule: R1 as defined in research/longscout_v1.py (100-day SMA of completed daily closes and its 20-day slope; rising / falling / sideways / unknown), read at each trade decision time (the entry bar open = the signal bar close), for BTC (market) and for the traded coin (own)
regime_check.runs: exp_trend rule v1 (max one, 40 orders) on extra31, and on the original nine (incl. BTC traded) with the same rule; all-order path trades saved
regime_check.report: per regime x side: closes, mean R15, sum R15 (order 0 and the median over 40 orders); share of time each regime holds; halves
regime_check.reading_frozen: structure reading = shorts earn mainly in falling regimes AND longs earn in rising ones (or at least do not lose); luck/one-regime dependence = the edge sits in one regime/period or one coin and the other side loses where it should win
